title: Returning from the seek phase
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine on Boolean input $x$, let $r$ be a natural number, and let $\mathrm{dec}:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$. Suppose an amplified-machine configuration $C$ is in the seek phase for run index $j\in\{0,\ldots,r\}$ and counter $c\in\{0,\ldots,r+1\}$, with input-head position $p\le |x|$. Every choice word of length at most $p+1$ leaves all work-tape head positions unchanged; every choice word of length exactly $p+1$ takes $C$ to the configuration obtained by restarting run $j$ at counter $c$, with the initial state and input-head position reset to their starting values while the other configuration data are retained.
